THE FOUNDATION BEHIND THE ASSISTANT

What is AI infrastructure?

AI infrastructure is the foundation that connects an AI assistant to the business information and software it needs. It includes the information sources, system connections, access permissions and operating rules that let the assistant support an agreed business task.

A useful assistant needs accurate information, a supported way to use your tools and a clear boundary around its actions. We scope those connections around a job your business needs done.

Approved business knowledge

Give the assistant an agreed source for your services, opening hours, common answers and rules. Decide who updates that information when the business changes.

Connections to your tools

Check how the assistant can read or update the calendar, customer system or job software you use. Define which system holds the authoritative record and which fields need to move.

Access and approval rules

Give each connection the permissions needed for its job. Decide which information the assistant may use, what it may change and which actions require a person’s approval.

A plan for exceptions

Agree how your team sees pending work, connection failures and requests outside the approved scope. Make responsibility for support and ongoing changes clear.

The tools below are examples to review for your setup. We check supported access, software plans and the actions you need before confirming a connection.

AN ILLUSTRATIVE BOOKING REQUEST

What does this mean in practice?

A customer calls to request a visit. The AI employee handles the conversation; the infrastructure provides the information and connections for the agreed next step.

  1. 01

    Collect the request

    The assistant captures the agreed details, such as the type of visit, contact information and preferred time.

  2. 02

    Check the right system

    If supported and authorised, the assistant checks connected availability or relevant customer information.

  3. 03

    Save the agreed outcome

    Booking rules determine whether a visit can be confirmed or must remain a request awaiting staff approval.

  4. 04

    Keep the team informed

    An agreed follow-up or handoff gives staff the next action. If a system is unavailable, the request follows the fallback plan.

This explains a possible setup, not a live integration or customer result. The actions available depend on your connected systems and agreed scope.

START WITH ONE CONNECTION THAT MATTERS

How we plan your AI infrastructure.

Start with a clear use case, then agree on the systems, information and responsibilities needed to support it.

  1. 01

    Map one useful outcome

    Choose a practical first task. List the information it needs, where that information lives and what a completed result should look like.

  2. 02

    Check access and compatibility

    Review the relevant software plans, connection methods and permissions. Confirm any limitations and separate provider charges before adding them to the scope.

  3. 03

    Test the whole path

    Review the normal case, missing information, staff approval and an unavailable system. Check how incomplete work is recorded and how duplicate actions are avoided where supported.

  4. 04

    Agree on ownership and updates

    Document the connected systems, permitted actions, team contact and support responsibilities. Your team should know how to change information or revoke a connection.

What to bring to the first conversation

  • The task you want the AI to help with.
  • The names and plans of your current phone, booking and customer systems.
  • Where your business information is kept and who maintains it.
  • The actions that need staff approval and a contact for exceptions.

PRACTICAL ANSWERS

Common questions about AI infrastructure.

Do we need to replace our current software?

We start with the tools you already use. The first step is to check their supported connections, your software plans and the information the AI needs. A new tool is considered when the existing setup cannot support the agreed task; replacement is not the starting assumption.

Can you connect tools such as Xero, Google Calendar or HubSpot?

The software shown on this page gives examples of systems we can assess. A connection depends on the provider’s supported access, your plan and permissions, and the exact action you want. We confirm compatibility and any limitations before including an integration in the scope.

Does AI infrastructure mean buying a server?

It does not necessarily require a physical server in your office. The design depends on your current systems, data requirements and the services needed for the task. Hosting and software requirements are agreed during scoping, together with ownership and ongoing costs.

How is infrastructure different from an AI employee or workflow?

An AI employee is the assistant’s business role, such as receptionist. AI infrastructure provides the information, software connections and access that role needs. An AI workflow is the agreed sequence of actions, such as collecting an enquiry, saving the details and notifying your team.

Where will our information be stored?

That depends on the software and hosting selected for your setup. Before connecting systems, agree which information is used, where it is processed or stored, who can access it and how long it is kept. New Zealand or Australia service coverage does not by itself mean that all data stays in those countries.

Who owns the accounts and controls access?

Account ownership, billing responsibility and administrator access should be explicit in the project scope. Connections should use approved authorisation and only the permissions needed for the task. Agree who can grant or revoke access and who maintains the setup after launch.

What happens if a connected system is unavailable?

We define the fallback before launch. Depending on the task, that may mean recording a pending request, notifying your team or asking a person to complete the step. Retries and duplicate checks should be considered where supported. A failed or pending action should not be presented to a caller as completed.

What affects the cost of an AI infrastructure setup?

Relevant factors include the number of systems, available connections, data preparation, permissions, testing and ongoing support. Software, phone and hosting providers may have separate charges. We scope a first use case and identify these costs before quoting; no fixed price or launch date is published on this page.
